units.translation: which the scholiast explains as "ἐπὶ τὴν εἰς ῞Αιδην ἀποικίαν ἑλκυσθήσεται μολεῖν τὴν ἐναντίαν τῇ εἰς Ἄργος [he will be dragged to the colony in Hades, to go the opposite way to Argos]". In most copies it is πόλιν [city].
ἥξουσ᾽ [she will come] Burges

Thus I corrected what is in M as πλέον [more], changed in inferior copies to παρόν [present], for which πέλον [being] could more probably be written. But πάλιν [back] seems more likely, considering the earlier events, which were described in the parodos of the chorus, from the words of the rising νεόκοτα θρέομαι φοβερὰ μεγάλ᾽ ἄχη [I cry out new, fearful, great griefs], where I supplied the word that had fallen out before θρέομαι [I cry out] by restoring νεόκοτα [new], a conjecture which this second passage so commends that it can be regarded as certain.

The scholiast explains it by ἡ ἐξ ὑστέρου όρμωμένη [that which starts up afterwards], other grammarians by ὀπισθόρμητος [rushing back]. The Homeric form of the adjective derived from ὄρω [to stir up] is παλίνορσος [rushing back], on which see Thes. vol. 6 p. 93. The other form παλίνορτος [rising again], to be compared with θέορτος [sprung from the gods], is judged more suitable to the etymology by Etym. M. p. 648, 27. But παλίνορτος [rising again] μῆνις [wrath] is said to refer to the crime committed by Atreus against the children of Thyestes, as Paleius noted.
